newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cop in Bhutto slay case dies mysteriously.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cop in Bhutto slay case dies mysteriously.

text.p: A member of the police squad involved in a fatal shootout with Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother died in mysterious circumstances on Saturday, the official APP news agency said.
It was not clear if Haq Nawaz Sial's death was a revenge killing for his role in last week's death in Karachi of Murtaza Bhutto and his seven bodyguards.
Unnamed police officials gave conflicting reports of how
"The wife of the deceased said that she saw two masked men fleeing from the house," one police official told Reuters.
Another senior police officer, who asked not to be named, said police were investigating, but "it appears a suicide case."
Sial "was shot dead under mysterious circumstances" in his home at the police headquarters early Saturday, APP said.

He was killed by "some unidentified assailants", it said. Murtaza Bhutto supporters have accused police of ambushing and killing him on September 20. Police say they fired in self-defence after Murtaza's bodyguards started shooting.
Two policemen, including Sial, suffered injuries.
A team of doctors investigating Murtaza's killing has said the wound suffered by Sial during the shootout was "self-inflicted".
The Sindh provincial government on Tuesday set up a medical board to investigate whether or not the wounds suffered by the policemen resulted from the shootout.

"The members of the team are of unanimous opinion that the left foot injury of Mr Haq Nawaz Sial of Clifton Police Station, Karachi has been caused by a firearm at close range and is self-suffered," a statement issued on Thursday by the Health Secretary of the government of Sindh province said.
